title: Impossible Love: Vintage Photographs

description.main: Catalogue of the C/O Berlin exhibition curated by Felix Hoffmann (December 2018 to March 2019), co-published with Steidl. It sets Nobuyoshi Araki's vintage Tokyo prints of 1969 to 1973 beside his recent Polaroid collages and slide shows in 368 pages and 319 plates, with texts in English and German.
description.extended:
Impossible Love: Vintage Photographs is the catalogue of the C/O Berlin exhibition that set Nobuyoshi Araki's own early prints of Tokyo, made between 1969 and 1973, beside the Polaroid collages and slide shows of his late work.

Steidl published it with C/O Berlin for the show curated by Felix Hoffmann, which ran from 8 December 2018 to 9 March 2019. The book has 368 pages and 319 plates, 97 in colour and 222 in black and white. It is a half-linen hardback with texts in English and German. The early section reproduces prints Araki made himself at the time of exposure. A young woman in a private room sits against office workers and passers-by on the street, the pairing he used in his first books to set the private and public conduct of Japanese society side by side. Some prints were torn, cut and reassembled by him, and they are reproduced as objects. The later section adds the Polaroid collages, the series Flower / Doll and Sky / Winds, and stills from slide shows made for the exhibition.

Araki (b. 1940, Tokyo) left the advertising agency Dentsu in 1972 and has published more than 500 books since. Vintage prints are scarce in an output of that size. This catalogue sits with the library's Dashwood and Taka Ishii Vintage Prints (2018), Theater of Love and Araki by Araki as the fullest account of his working prints from the formative years.
description.artist_bio: Nobuyoshi Araki (b. 1940, Tokyo) studied photography and film at Chiba University and worked at the advertising agency Dentsu until 1972. Sentimental Journey (1971), the diary of his honeymoon with Yoko Aoki, set the intimate, diaristic mode he has followed since across more than 500 books, including the Tokyo street series of the early 1970s, Tokyo Lucky Hole, and the later flower, bondage and sky series.
description.exhibition_context: Nobuyoshi Araki. Impossible Love: Vintage Photographs, C/O Berlin, Amerika Haus, 8 December 2018 to 9 March 2019 (C/O Berlin's listed end date; Steidl and Artbook give 3 March 2019), curated by Felix Hoffmann. The show paired previously unpublished early series with Flower / Doll, Sky / Winds, Polaroid collages and new slide shows.
